job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
Project Manager

Location: Andover area, Hampshire (Weyhill vicinity)

The Opportunity

We are looking for a driven Project Manager to join our fast-paced defence and engineering projects team. This role is perfect for someone who loves the challenge of taking full ownership of small-to-medium defence projects (£1m–£15m) and turning complex client requirements into a structured, successful reality. You will spend your days balancing rigorous technical compliance and quality standards with real-world commercial goals.

In this role, you will be the bridge between our customers, design engineers, and manufacturing teams. Working alongside the Programme Director, you will lead high-profile projects, guiding them from contract flow-down right through to final delivery, while helping to build and expand our internal project management function.

  • Own project execution: As our designated Project Manager, you will solely manage the day-to-day delivery of large defence projects from concept to final manufacture.
  • Control the financials & schedule: Take full accountability for financial performance, tracking actuals against forecasts and managing MS Project schedules.
  • Manage client & partner relationships: Guide complex stakeholder expectations, manage sub-contractors, and identify follow-on business opportunities.
  • Mitigate project risks: Identify, monitor, and resolve daily challenges relating to quality, costs, supply chain, and resource demands.
  • Drive process & governance: Implement defined project lifecycle processes and provide clear monthly progress reporting to executive leadership.

About You

You are a results-driven leader who understands how to navigate complex, highly regulated environments. You thrive in a collaborative workspace, bring excellent commercial and technical astuteness, and have the following to your name:

  • Defence industry experience: A strong background working within a technical defence environment as a Project Manager, ideally including familiarity with MoD acquisition processes.
  • Technical project know-how: Advanced capability with MS Project, Excel, and engineering lifecycle governance. Experience with MRP systems or ISO 9001 internal auditing is a major plus.

job.title: Manufacturing Engineer
job.description:

The Opportunity
We are looking for a proficient and driven Manufacturing Engineer to join our expanding Industrialisation Department on a contract basis. This role is perfect for a process-minded contractor who thrives on bridging the gap between product design and real-world production. You will take hands-on ownership of developing, improving, and optimising complex mechanical manufacturing processes across a variety of high-performance engineering projects.
As a Manufacturing Engineer, you will be the vital link between our engineering, quality assurance, and assembly teams. Working at the forefront of high-precision electro-mechanical systems, you will ensure our advanced products are introduced into production on time, to cost, and to the highest quality standards, driving lean efficiencies while supporting the implementation of rigorous Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) processes.

  • Drive technical documentation: Produce and maintain critical APQP and PPAP documentation, including process flows, PFMEAs, control plans, work instructions, and MSA capability studies.
  • Manage the Build Blueprint: Check the accuracy of Engineering Bills of Materials (EBOM) against build requirements and convert them into functional Production Bills of Materials (PBOM).
  • Direct tooling & supplier sourcing: Conduct make-vs-buy analyses, identify tooling and equipment requirements for new assembly lines, and write technical specification documents for supplier quotations.
  • Support program milestones: Lead PFMEA reviews to drive process improvements and support the wider program team in delivering key industrialisation and stage-gate milestones.
About You
You are a highly collaborative, process-driven engineer with a strong commitment to quality improvement and a methodical approach to problem-solving. To succeed as our new Manufacturing Engineer, you must excel in a dynamic environment, bring a deep understanding of complex assembly processes, and have the following to your name:
  • Industry experience: Significant engineering experience within a safety-critical, highly regulated manufacturing environment (such as aerospace, automotive, or medical devices).
  • Technical standards know-how: A solid understanding of design for manufacture/assembly (DFMA) principles and quality frameworks, specifically APQP, PPAP, PFMEA, SPC, and MSA.
  • CAD capability: Practical ability to interpret 2D technical drawings and interrogate 3D CAD modeling software.
  • Organisational foundation: Excellent project management, communication, and leadership skills to effectively manage deadlines and collaborate across cross-functional teams.
  • Desirable extras: Previous experience training trainees, leading root cause analysis sessions, and managing industrialisation timing plans.
What Success Looks Like
When you settle into the role, success as a Manufacturing Engineer will mean seamlessly launching new production processes with zero disruption to industrialisation timelines. You will become a trusted technical advisor across design and quality teams, ensuring manufacturing safety regulations are flawlessly maintained and that our electro-mechanical systems are produced with optimal efficiency, reduced costs, and maximum reliability.

Certification and Testing Engineer

Location: Sidcup area, Greater London area

We are looking for a meticulous Certification and Testing Engineer to join our dedicated product compliance team. You will spend your days balancing complex international standards with practical product design goals.

In this role, you will be the vital link between our internal design teams and external UKAS-accredited laboratories. Working at the forefront of passive fire protection as a Certification and Testing Engineer, you will ensure our lifesaving products maintain total compliance with UK, European, and international regulations while helping to support exciting new product development.

What You Will Do Day-to-Day

  • Own the testing pipeline: Assist with the planning, coordination, and preparation of rigorous fire resistance and smoke control testing programmes.
  • Prepare samples & details: Support the build preparation, specifications, and physical product sampling for external test house audits.
  • Manage external relationships: Liaise directly with certification bodies and test houses, such as third-party UKAS laboratories.
  • Drive technical documentation: Prepare and maintain critical technical data sheets, declarations, fire test reports, assessments, and certification documents.
  • Collaborate on design: Work closely with CAD, Product, and Design teams to ensure all manufactured configurations perfectly reflect tested constructions.
  • Monitor compliance standards: Keep a close eye on regulatory updates, supporting compliance activities for standards including BS 476, EN 1634, and UL.

About You

You are a process-driven professional with a high attention to detail and a methodical approach to compliance. To succeed as our new Certification and Testing Engineer, you must thrive in an environment where accuracy is paramount, bring excellent technical understanding, and have the following to your name:

  • Industry experience: A strong understanding of fire testing and compliance processes within the construction, doorset, joinery, or passive fire protection sectors.
  • Technical standards know-how: Familiarity with relevant regulatory frameworks, specifically BS 476-22/31.1, EN 1634-1, UL 10C, and UL 1784.
  • CAD capability: Practical experience producing and amending 2D and 3D technical CAD drawings to support testing and certification details.
  • Organisational foundation: Strong written communication skills to produce clear, structured technical documentation, alongside the ability to manage multiple strict deadlines.
  • Desirable extras: Previous experience with Factory Production Control (FPC) audit processes, joinery product development, or change control activities is a major plus.

What Success Looks Like

When you settle into the role, success as a Certification and Testing Engineer will mean seamlessly coordinating complex fire testing programmes with zero disruption to compliance timelines. You will become a trusted technical advisor to our design and production teams, ensuring our technical library is flawlessly maintained and our products remain fully certified to the highest international safety standards.

What We Offer

  • Competitive package: A rewarding salary tailored to your specific testing and passive fire protection experience.
  • Critical safety impact: The chance to take ownership of testing programmes for high-performance products that directly protect human lives.
  • Growth and development: Deep exposure to international certification schemes and leading-edge passive fire engineering.
